j1.why: Step 1: v4 has no caught-up signal. Step 2: STATUS.md records that a member back inside the eviction window says writable about 100 ms before it holds its peers' rows. Step 3: that run is this requirement's own regression test, so v4 as it is fails it; the per-peer tails that could fix it sit unused in kernel/confirm.ts.

j2.why: v4 has the fault today: a member back inside the eviction window says writable about 100 ms before it holds its peers' rows (STATUS.md). The per-peer tails the signal needs are already in kernel/confirm.ts, so it is a missing report, not a limit of the design.
j2.closes: a public caught-up signal in v4, with the regression test

j1.why: The design applies a seed once, at create, and marks it in the catalog (`#meta`'s resource record), so a joining copy takes its state from the log and never runs its own seed. No experiment modelled the create with its seed: a crash between the catalog record and the seed rows, or two servers that create at once.
j1.closes: v4's revived-seed-row case as a regression test in the phase-1 sim, with a crash between create and seed and two creators at once

j2.why: A resource is made by one committed catalog entry, and its seed is written once through the group's log, with 'seed applied' kept in the catalog row (DESIGN-V5 §4.2). A joining copy folds the log or a snapshot and never writes a seed of its own, and one log per group means a removed row cannot come back from another copy. E-33 shows a project founds one cluster with A-08.

j1.why: Step 1: v4 collects a deleted row's tombstone within a heartbeat. Step 2: a fresh member applies every seed key its empty fold lacks ('fresh keys ride in'). Step 3: it cannot tell a deleted key from one the cluster never had, so the seed row comes back and LWW spreads it. STATUS.md: 2 runs of 2 on v4 63e0679, and every scale-out of a seeded resource hits it.

j2.why: v4 fails the regression today: a fresh member's seed brings back a row the cluster deleted, in 2 runs of 2 (STATUS.md), because LWW with collected tombstones cannot tell 'never had' from 'deleted'. J's fix, a joining copy skips its seed, fits v4's join by ballot and is not built.
j2.closes: the skip-seed-on-join fix in v4, with the regression test

j1.why: Parts are measured: a prototype client reaches its first committed write over one wss address in 13 to 17 ms (E-40), and a TLS terminator stands in front of a TS edge because 10,000 TLS links cost 538 MB in Node (E-27, A-11). No test sent clients through one proxy address to several copies, where a write must be forwarded to its leader; a `smart` row needs a proxy that routes by a hint, which nobody examined (G-25).
j1.closes: the client test through one proxy address on the phase-3 build (TLS terminator, forward to the leader)

j2.why: Any server takes a client's write and forwards it to the group's leader (Y `fwd`; the `smart` rows keep `fwd` for browsers), and reads come from any ready replica or are passed on, so one public address in front of the copies reaches every resource. E-40 measured a client on one wss address reaching its first committed write in 13 to 17 ms. A TS edge takes a TLS terminator in front (A-11; E-27: 538 MB for 10,000 TLS links without one).
